proof_attempt_summary: Established the uniformly matched blind/disclosed/clean W1 testing frontier over the compact latent-outcome, common iid raw-second-moment error class, with a periodic modulus, weighted-trace upper certificate, and normalized Gaussian complete-record converse. Independent mathematical review and boundary/terminal consultations found the theorem sound, including both repeat-count transitions and the arbitrary-sequence clean-order criterion. The delivered package is subfield against a field floor because its conservative constants and astronomical n0 provide no practical planning guarantee and there is no implementation or finite-sample power study; comparator provenance and unconsumed signal-domain ballast remain explicitly unresolved. Formalization did not start, so no Lean certificate, promoted substrate, or acceptance is claimed.
tldr: Theorem \texttt{thm:sharp-repeat-count-frontier} proves the matched blind, disclosed-noise and clean testing frontier for \(\theta(P)=W_1(\mu_1(P),\mu_0(P))\) on the entire primitive class \(\mathcal M\). Potential-outcome marginals are arbitrary laws on \([-1,1]\), including atoms; readings have a common iid additive error law satisfying \(\int x^2\,d\eta(x)\le1\), without error-location normalization. The tests have finite-sample null size at most \(0.05\), with stated nonrejection fallbacks, and the converse compares the complete marked reading-vector experiment. The evaluated rates satisfy \(r_{\mathrm b}=r_{\mathrm d}\): disclosure yields no unbounded worst-class rate improvement. For every integer repeat sequence, blind and disclosed radii are of clean order \(r_{\mathrm c}(n)=n^{-1/2}\) if and only if \(\liminf_{n\to\infty}p_n\log n/n>0\). The two elbows occur at \(p\asymp\log n\) and \(p\asymp n/\log n\). This is a different distributional causal testing frontier motivated by repeated-measurement density estimation; it does not solve the anchor's density-estimation question.
